newsitem.title: USA: Energy stocks seen gaining ground - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Energy stocks seen gaining ground - Barron's.

text.p: Energy stocks, after suffering a beating in the first three or four months of this year, are quietly recuperating some of their lost ground, said columnist Alan Abelson in the May 19 issue of Barron's.

In his "Up & Down Wall Street" column, Abelson cites analyst Tom Petrie of Denver-based Petrie Parkman, who, while expressing a "restrained view of the outlook for prices for oil and gas", is bullish on the energy group.
Petrie's picks are Barrett Resources Corp, Flores & Rucks Inc and United Meridian Corp.

The article said Petrie was upbeat on Barrett's management and an onshore gas project in Wyoming. He estimates earnings at around $0.92 per share for this year and $1.55 next year, and expects the stock to reach $48 within 12 months. It closed at 32-1/4 on Friday.
Petrie sees Flores & Rucks earning $1.95 per share this year and $2.95 in 1998. He sees the stock, which closed at 49-1/4 on Friday, hitting $65 within a year.
United Meridian will probably have around an $0.08 per share loss this year, but Petrie sees earnings of $2.10 a share next year.
